quests.instruction: Write a short, natural answer to the prompt below, using all three key words.
quests.prompt: Write about the difference between a claim that must be true by pure logic and one that depends on real-world evidence.
quests.sampleAnswer: A claim that must be true by pure logic needs no outside evidence, unlike a claim whose truth depends entirely on how the world happens to be.
quests.hint: Define the first type of claim using 'needs no', then define the second type using 'depends on'.
quests.explanation: Contrasting 'needs no outside evidence' with 'depends entirely on how the world happens to be' draws a clean, useful line between two very different kinds of truth.

quests.instruction: Write a short, natural answer to the prompt below, using all three key words.
quests.prompt: Write about how Hawking radiation causes black holes to slowly lose mass and eventually evaporate.
quests.sampleAnswer: Hawking radiation causes black holes to slowly evaporate by emitting thermal radiation at a temperature inversely proportional to their mass.
quests.hint: Name the phenomenon and what it causes black holes to do, then specify how temperature relates to mass.
quests.explanation: 'Inversely proportional to their mass' names the precise relationship - smaller black holes are hotter and evaporate faster.

quests.instruction: Write a short, natural answer to the prompt below, using all three key words.
quests.prompt: Write about how people sometimes deny their own freedom and responsibility to avoid a difficult choice.
quests.sampleAnswer: People sometimes deny their own freedom to avoid the responsibility that comes with truly owning a difficult choice.
quests.hint: State what people sometimes deny, then explain what they're trying to avoid by denying it.
quests.explanation: Linking denial to avoiding 'responsibility that comes with truly owning a difficult choice' captures a real and relatable psychological pattern.

quests.instruction: Write a short, natural answer to the prompt below, using all three key words.
quests.prompt: Write about how a clear structural outline helps organize a long piece of writing before you draft a single sentence.
quests.sampleAnswer: A clear structural outline helps writers organize a long piece before drafting, mapping how every part will relate to the whole.
quests.hint: Name the planning tool, then explain what it helps writers do before they start drafting.
quests.explanation: 'Mapping how every part will relate to the whole' is the real value of an outline - it solves structural problems before they become expensive to fix.

quests.instruction: Write a short, natural answer to the prompt below, using all three key words.
quests.prompt: Write about how engineers calculate the absolute limit on how much data a communication channel can carry.
quests.sampleAnswer: Engineers calculate the theoretical limit on how much data a communication channel can carry before errors become unavoidable.
quests.hint: Name what engineers calculate, then specify what happens once that limit is crossed.
quests.explanation: 'Before errors become unavoidable' names the real constraint - every channel has a ceiling, no matter how good the technology.

quests.instruction: Write a short, natural answer to the prompt below, using all three key words.
quests.prompt: Write about why forcing a messy, complicated situation into one simple category can distort the truth.
quests.sampleAnswer: Forcing a messy, complicated situation into one simple category can distort the truth by erasing exactly the details that mattered most.
quests.hint: State what forcing a situation into one category can do, then explain exactly what gets lost.
quests.explanation: 'Erasing exactly the details that mattered most' is the real cost of oversimplification - the parts that don't fit are often the most important ones.

quests.instruction: Write a short, natural answer to the prompt below, using all three key words.
quests.prompt: Write about why expert writers choose one precise word instead of a wordy, roundabout phrase.
quests.sampleAnswer: Expert writers choose one precise word instead of a wordy, roundabout phrase that only dilutes their meaning.
quests.hint: State what expert writers choose, then contrast it with the wordy alternative they avoid.
quests.explanation: Calling the alternative 'wordy' and 'roundabout' emphasizes the cost of imprecision - readers have to work harder to extract the same meaning.

quests.instruction: Write a short, natural answer to the prompt below, using all three key words.
quests.prompt: Write about how researchers map the complex web of interactions between proteins inside a living cell.
quests.sampleAnswer: Researchers map the complex web of protein interactions inside a living cell to understand how its systems actually function.
quests.hint: Name what researchers map inside a cell, then state the ultimate purpose of doing so.
quests.explanation: 'Understand how its systems actually function' names the payoff - mapping interactions reveals function that studying single proteins alone would miss.

quests.instruction: Write a short, natural answer to the prompt below, using all three key words.
quests.prompt: Write about how the true meaning of a word often becomes clear only through watching how people actually use it.
quests.sampleAnswer: The true meaning of a word often becomes clear only through watching how people actually use it in real conversation.
quests.hint: State when a word's true meaning becomes clear, then specify where you have to look to see it.
quests.explanation: 'In real conversation' is the key phrase - it grounds an abstract question about meaning in something every reader has direct experience with.

quests.instruction: Write a short, natural answer to the prompt below, using all three key words.
quests.prompt: Write about why the best essays explore a genuine tension in their topic instead of pretending it doesn't exist.
quests.sampleAnswer: The best essays explore a genuine tension in their topic instead of pretending it doesn't exist or smoothing it over.
quests.hint: State what the best essays do with tension in their topic, then contrast this with two weaker alternatives.
quests.explanation: Naming two weak alternatives ('pretending it doesn't exist or smoothing it over') makes the stronger choice - genuinely engaging the tension - feel earned by comparison.

quests.instruction: Write a short, natural answer to the prompt below, using all three key words.
quests.prompt: Write about how inflationary cosmology explains the remarkable uniformity of the observable universe.
quests.sampleAnswer: Inflationary cosmology proposes the early universe underwent rapid expansion, an inflation that smoothed initial inhomogeneities.
quests.hint: Name the theory, then describe the early-universe event and its effect on uniformity.
quests.explanation: 'Smoothed initial inhomogeneities' is the precise consequence - inflation explains the uniformity of the early universe.

quests.instruction: Write a short, natural answer to the prompt below, using all three key words.
quests.prompt: Write about how a single unexpected event can suddenly make something possible that seemed impossible before.
quests.sampleAnswer: A single unexpected event can suddenly make something possible that had seemed completely impossible only moments before.
quests.hint: State what kind of event can do this, then contrast the before-and-after using 'possible' and 'impossible'.
quests.explanation: Contrasting 'possible' and 'impossible' in one sentence captures the dramatic, sudden nature of the shift being described.

quests.instruction: Write a short, natural answer to the prompt below, using all three key words.
quests.prompt: Write about why a single disappointing experimental result rarely overturns an entire well-supported scientific theory.
quests.sampleAnswer: A single disappointing result rarely overturns an entire well-supported scientific theory, since one anomaly is usually explained away first.
quests.hint: State what a single result rarely does to a well-supported theory, then explain what usually happens to that result first.
quests.explanation: 'Usually explained away first' captures a realistic pattern in science - a lone anomaly gets scrutinized before it's allowed to threaten an established theory.

quests.instruction: Write a short, natural answer to the prompt below, using all three key words.
quests.prompt: Write about how scientists compare gene activity between a healthy sample and a diseased one to find meaningful differences.
quests.sampleAnswer: Scientists compare gene activity between a healthy sample and a diseased one to identify the difference that actually matters.
quests.hint: Name the two samples being compared, then state what scientists are trying to identify.
quests.explanation: 'The difference that actually matters' is precise - the goal isn't just noticing differences, but isolating the ones connected to the disease.

quests.instruction: Write a short, natural answer to the prompt below, using all three key words.
quests.prompt: Write about why some news stories about tragedy receive far more public attention and sympathy than others.
quests.sampleAnswer: Some stories of tragedy receive far more public sympathy and attention than others, often for reasons that have little to do with the scale of suffering.
quests.hint: State what some tragedies receive more of than others, then comment on whether this always tracks the actual scale of suffering.
quests.explanation: Noting the gap 'has little to do with the scale of suffering' invites a genuinely important question about which stories the media and public choose to elevate.

quests.instruction: Write a short, natural answer to the prompt below, using all three key words.
quests.prompt: Write about how breaking a complicated idea into its basic parts can make it easier to define clearly.
quests.sampleAnswer: To break down a complicated idea into its basic parts often makes it far easier to define clearly and precisely.
quests.hint: State what breaking an idea into parts does, then describe the effect on clarity.
quests.explanation: This is a foundational thinking strategy across many fields - complexity becomes manageable once you isolate and name the individual pieces.

quests.instruction: Write a short, natural answer to the prompt below, using all three key words.
quests.prompt: Write about how the many-worlds interpretation of quantum mechanics posits branching parallel universes.
quests.sampleAnswer: The many-worlds interpretation posits that every quantum measurement causes branching into parallel, non-communicating universes.
quests.hint: Name the interpretation, then describe what happens to the universe at every quantum measurement.
quests.explanation: 'Non-communicating universes' is the key phrase - once the branches separate, they cannot interact with one another again.

quests.instruction: Write a short, natural answer to the prompt below, using all three key words.
quests.prompt: Write about how a person's name still refers to them even in an imagined situation where every fact about their life is different.
quests.sampleAnswer: A person's name still refers to them even in an imagined situation where every single fact about their life is different.
quests.hint: State what still works even in an imagined scenario, then specify how much about that scenario has changed.
quests.explanation: This is a genuinely strange and interesting puzzle about language - it shows that names can behave differently from ordinary descriptions.

quests.instruction: Write a short, natural answer to the prompt below, using all three key words.
quests.prompt: Write about how a strong closing paragraph can leave the reader with a clear sense of the writer's confidence in their argument.
quests.sampleAnswer: A strong closing paragraph leaves the reader with a clear sense of the writer's confidence in the argument just made.
quests.hint: Name what a strong closing leaves the reader with, then specify whose confidence it reflects.
quests.explanation: Ending on a note of 'clear confidence' matters - readers remember how an argument concludes more than how carefully it hedged along the way.

quests.instruction: Write a short, natural answer to the prompt below, using all three key words.
quests.prompt: Write about how different regions of the brain must work together in coordination to produce complex thought.
quests.sampleAnswer: Different regions of the brain must coordinate closely with one another to produce genuinely complex thought and behavior.
quests.hint: Name what different brain regions must do together, then specify the kind of thought this produces.
quests.explanation: This reflects a key shift in neuroscience - complex thought isn't located in one single brain area, it emerges from coordination across many.

quests.instruction: Write a short, natural answer to the prompt below, using all three key words.
quests.prompt: Write about why people today are often more skeptical of big, sweeping explanations for how the world works.
quests.sampleAnswer: People today are often more skeptical of sweeping explanations that claim to account for how the entire world works.
quests.hint: State how people tend to react to big explanations today, then describe the scope such explanations claim to cover.
quests.explanation: Describing explanations as 'sweeping' hints at the reason for the skepticism - the bigger and neater the claim, the more it invites careful scrutiny.

quests.instruction: Write a short, natural answer to the prompt below, using all three key words.
quests.prompt: Write about how expert prose transmits the maximum amount of information using the minimum number of words.
quests.sampleAnswer: Expert prose achieves maximum information transfer using minimum words, so that not a single word feels wasted.
quests.hint: State what expert prose achieves in terms of information and word count, then add a result clause about waste.
quests.explanation: 'Not a single word feels wasted' is the real test of economical prose - every word should be doing real work in the sentence.

quests.instruction: Write a short, natural answer to the prompt below, using all three key words.
quests.prompt: Write about how the cosmological constant serves as the leading explanation for the accelerating expansion of the universe.
quests.sampleAnswer: The cosmological constant is the leading explanation for the accelerating expansion of the universe observed at the largest cosmic scales.
quests.hint: Use 'The cosmological constant is the leading theoretical explanation for the observed accelerating expansion of the universe at' and end.
quests.explanation: 'At the largest cosmic scales' scopes the claim precisely - the acceleration is only measurable across vast intergalactic distances.

quests.instruction: Write a short, natural answer to the prompt below, using all three key words.
quests.prompt: Write about how two different descriptions can refer to the exact same real-world thing without anyone realizing it at first.
quests.sampleAnswer: Two different descriptions can refer to the exact same real-world thing without anyone realizing it until much later.
quests.hint: State what two different descriptions can share, then specify how long it can take for anyone to notice.
quests.explanation: 'Until much later' captures something genuinely interesting about language and discovery - two labels can quietly point at one thing for a long time before anyone connects them.

quests.instruction: Write a short, natural answer to the prompt below, using all three key words.
quests.prompt: Write about how a well-crafted concluding sentence can clinch an argument by revealing its inevitable implication.
quests.sampleAnswer: The final sentence clinches the argument by revealing its most important implication as logically inevitable and practically urgent.
quests.hint: State what the final sentence does to the argument, then describe the implication with two adjectives.
quests.explanation: 'Logically inevitable and practically urgent' names two types of force: intellectual necessity and real-world consequence.

quests.instruction: Write a short, natural answer to the prompt below, using all three key words.
quests.prompt: Write about a surprising scientific idea: that all the information about a space could theoretically be described using only its outer surface.
quests.sampleAnswer: One surprising scientific idea proposes that all the information within a space could theoretically be described using only its outer surface.
quests.hint: Introduce the idea as surprising, then state what could theoretically be described using only a surface.
quests.explanation: Calling the idea 'surprising' is honest framing - reducing a description of a whole space down to just its surface defies ordinary intuition.

quests.instruction: Write a short, natural answer to the prompt below, using all three key words.
quests.prompt: Write about how an old idea can be refined by a new one without being completely thrown away in the process.
quests.sampleAnswer: A good new idea can refine an old one without the old one being simply thrown away in the process.
quests.hint: State what a good new idea can do to an old one, then clarify what does NOT happen to the old idea.
quests.explanation: Clarifying what does not happen (the old idea being thrown away) is a precise way to describe genuine intellectual progress, as opposed to simple replacement.

quests.instruction: Write a short, natural answer to the prompt below, using all three key words.
quests.prompt: Write about how a master chef can take a traditional recipe and transform it into something genuinely original.
quests.sampleAnswer: A master chef can take a traditional recipe passed down for generations and transform it into something genuinely original.
quests.hint: Name the kind of expert, then describe what they do to a traditional recipe.
quests.explanation: Using a concrete example (a master chef and a recipe) makes an abstract claim about mastery and innovation immediately easy to picture, in any discipline.

quests.instruction: Write a short, natural answer to the prompt below, using all three key words.
quests.prompt: Write about why final-round negotiators often make their biggest concessions only when a deadline is about to expire.
quests.sampleAnswer: Negotiators often save their biggest concessions for the very end, offering them only as a deadline is about to expire.
quests.hint: State when negotiators tend to make their biggest concessions, then specify the exact timing that triggers this.
quests.explanation: This is a well-documented negotiation pattern - a ticking deadline creates pressure that unlocks flexibility neither side showed earlier in the conversation.

quests.instruction: Write a short, natural answer to the prompt below, using all three key words.
quests.prompt: Write about why nothing in nature can be fully understood in complete isolation from everything around it.
quests.sampleAnswer: Nothing in nature can be fully understood in isolation, since every living thing exists as part of a deeply interconnected system.
quests.hint: State what can't be understood alone, then explain what larger system every living thing belongs to.
quests.explanation: This ecological insight applies far beyond biology - systems thinking, in general, reminds us that context and relationship often matter as much as the thing itself.
